description.narrative: Contribution to market Creation: Resilience: IFC anticipates that the Project will contribute to the resilience of Ghanas cocoa sector currently affected by limited adequate finance straining the ability of traders to sustain cocoa sourcing from farmers and that could ultimately affect Ghanas ability to maintain its global market position as a major supplier of cocoa. To monitor progress against this outcome, IFC will track the number of private sector participants benefiting from the project and monitor the total value of cocoa exported by Ghana. Project outcome: Stakeholder effects: Increased Access to Finance: IFC anticipates that the facility will increase liquidity in the agri supply chain and access to finance for farmers by providing the participating banks with an efficient and competitive risk mitigating tool to accept a higher degree of lending risk. Credit to Ghanas agricultural sector is even lower relative to the contribution it makes to the countrys GDP, where many lenders lack the risk tolerance and/or expertise to lend to small holder farmers The project is expected to reach over139,000 farmers in the value chain of the LBCs. To monitor progress against this outcome, IFC will track the volumes of US$ commodities financed by the facility and volumes of MT cocoa trade supported.

The proposed investment consists of an unfunded risk participation facility of up to US$61 million to Access Bank Ghana PLC (Access Bank Ghana). The facility is part of a broader syndicated package supporting four Ghanaian banks to finance the purchase of traceable cocoa beans from smallholder farmers via leading Licensed Buying Companies (LBCs). The facility will be used to provide working capital to six major LBCs: AgroECOM & Unicom/ECOM, Nyonkopa/Barry Callebaut, Eliho/TOUTON, FedCo/SUCDEN & Barry Callebaut, CJ Commodities/SUCDEN, and Adikanfo/SUCDEN.
